articles.title: Seat Turns Battleground: Women Brawl Inside AP RTC Bus in Anantapur

The incident occurred on Tuesday in an RTC bus travelling from Uravakonda Mandal to Kanekal village.

body.html:
A heated clash broke out among women passengers over a seat inside an Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) bus in Anantapur district, creating chaos during the journey.

The incident occurred on Tuesday in an RTC bus travelling from Uravakonda Mandal to Kanekal village. According to eyewitnesses, several women began arguing over a seat, which soon escalated into verbal abuse and physical assault. Other passengers were left shocked as the scuffle continued inside the moving bus.

Incidents of quarrels over seats in RTC buses have reportedly become frequent, with overcrowding often triggering such clashes. No injuries were reported in the latest incident, and further details are awaited.

articles.title: ‘Dhoom-3 Style’ Twin Brothers Lead Two-Wheeler Theft Gang, 15 Bikes Recovered
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Police have busted a gang of vehicle thieves and arrested four accused, including identical twin brothers who allegedly masterminded the crimes by exploiting their striking resemblance to evade identification.

body.html:
Police have busted a gang of vehicle thieves and arrested four accused, including identical twin brothers who allegedly masterminded the crimes by exploiting their striking resemblance to evade identification.

The arrested accused have been identified as Shadab alias Rutba, twin brothers Arman alias Sutta and Ulman, and Vijay. They were arrested on Monday near Sector-14A. Police recovered 15 stolen two-wheelers and a large quantity of vehicle parts, including 12 fuel tanks, five silencers, five masks, four mudguards and two tyre rims. The total value of the recovered property is estimated at around ₹15 lakh.

According to police, the gang’s unique modus operandi involved the identical twins wearing similar clothes and switching roles to mislead investigators. While one brother would remain at a shop, the other would carry out thefts, making it difficult for police and victims to identify the culprit.

During investigation, police found that the gang conducted reconnaissance of two-wheelers parked near colonies, societies, factories and company premises across Delhi, Noida, NCR and nearby areas. The accused would break the locks and steal the vehicles, which were later dismantled at scrap shops and sold as spare parts, or sold cheaply in other states.

Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Khatushyamji Police Bust Massive Family Gang: 18 Arrested for Chain Snatching on New Year
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Amid a rise in chain-snatching incidents in Khatushyamji, Sikar police have cracked down on an organised gang and arrested 18 accused, including husbands, wives and close relatives.

body.html:
Amid a rise in chain-snatching incidents in Khatushyamji, Sikar police have cracked down on an organised gang and arrested 18 accused, including husbands, wives and close relatives. The arrests followed a meticulously planned operation during New Year celebrations, which ensured that not a single chain-snatching incident was reported despite heavy crowds.

Station House Officer (SHO) Pawan Kumar Choubey said that several incidents of chain snatching and pickpocketing had earlier been reported during Ekadashi and monthly fairs. Learning from past cases, a special strategy was drawn up for New Year in coordination with DST team in-charge Virendra Yadav, Kailash Chand Yadav and other police personnel.

Considering the large influx of devotees, police personnel in plainclothes were deployed from the temple entry points to the exit areas. Based on the modus operandi seen in previous crimes, suspicious movements were closely monitored. The gang members were detained from the crowd and later confessed to their involvement during interrogation.

According to police, the gang had been active in Khatushyamji for the past seven to eight months. They would arrive every month on crowded days like Ekadashi in rented vehicles, target devotees in congested areas such as the temple exit and main complex, and flee immediately after committing the crime, often escaping detection due to the rush.

Police said the crimes were executed primarily by women. The women would move in groups, surround victims, engage them in conversation and snatch gold chains. The stolen jewellery was either quickly passed on to male accomplices or the women would flee, making recovery difficult even if they were caught.

Those arrested include Bhumika (20), wife of Deepak; Pinky (27), wife of Manoj Bawaria; Pooja (28), wife of Sonu; Tina (29), wife of Vikas; Sharmila (37), wife of Ramchandra; Jyoti (30), wife of Rajkumar; Kajal (20), daughter of Sundarlal; Rakhi Kumari (23), daughter of Ramesh; Darshana (40), wife of Raju; Komal (22), daughter of Ramanand; Jaipal (62), son of Chandrabhan; Rajkumar (30), son of Jaipal; Jaikaran (34), son of Ramesh; Mohan Singh (24), son of Bhup Singh; Deepak (22), son of Raju; Bharatpal (21), son of Rajesh; Rohit (24), son of Kishanpal; and Praveen Chauhan (23), son of Umed Singh. The accused are residents of Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi-NCR, and belong to the same extended family network.

SHO Choubey stated that despite massive crowds on New Year’s Day, no chain-snatching incident occurred due to heightened vigilance and coordinated policing. The gang was apprehended as part of a planned operation carried out within the crowd.

articles.title: Land Greed Turns Killer: Man Murders Father, Sister and 14-Year-Old Niece, Dumps Bodies in Well
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Prayagraj: A shocking triple murder over a land dispute has come to light in Lokpur Bisani village under the Mauaima police station area of Prayagraj.

body.html:
Prayagraj: A shocking triple murder over a land dispute has come to light in Lokpur Bisani village under the Mauaima police station area of Prayagraj. Ram Singh (55), his daughter Sadhana Devi (21) and granddaughter Aastha (14) were reported missing on the night of Friday, January 2, 2026.

Early on Saturday, January 3, the accused, Mukesh Patel, allegedly shot his younger brother Mukund Patel in the neck, seriously injuring him. Mukund survived and later named Mukesh as the prime suspect.

Police said that on the same day and night, Mukesh entered his father’s house, strangled Ram Singh and attacked Sadhana and Aastha with an axe, killing all three. Taking advantage of dense night fog, he dumped their bodies into a nearby 20-foot-deep well.

On Sunday, January 4, Mukund Patel lodged a missing persons report at Mauaima police station, clearly suspecting his elder brother Mukesh. After a two-day search operation, which included drone surveillance, a joint team of Mauaima police, Special Operations Group (SOG) and the Crime Branch arrested Mukesh Patel on Monday, January 5.

During interrogation, Mukesh confessed to the murders and led police to the well, from where the bodies of Ram Singh, Sadhana Devi and Aastha were recovered. Police also seized the murder weapons, including an axe and a country-made pistol with two cartridges.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (Ganga Nagar) Kuldeep Gunawat said the motive behind the crime was a long-standing land dispute. About a year ago, Ram Singh had transferred his house and around four to 4.5 bighas of land to his younger son Mukund, excluding Mukesh. The accused had reportedly demanded an additional 10 biswas of land, and his resentment grew after his father refused. The disputed property is estimated to be worth ₹1–1.5 crore.

ACP Vivek Yadav of Phulpur confirmed that multiple police teams were involved in the investigation and legal proceedings are underway. Bloodstains were found at the house, and all recoveries were made based on the accused’s confession.

An FIR has been registered at Mauaima police station under murder charges. The bodies were sent for post-mortem examination, and Mukesh Patel has been remanded in custody. Police said further action will follow based on forensic reports and ongoing investigation.

The brutal killings have shocked residents of Lokpur Bisani village, with locals expressing disbelief that a man could murder his own family over a property dispute.

articles.title: Jhansi’s First Woman Auto Driver Shot Dead, Murder Made to Look Like Accident: Family
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Jhansi’s first female auto driver, Anita Chaudhary (40), was found dead in a pool of blood near her overturned auto-rickshaw in the Navabad police station area early Sunday morning, triggering shock and outrage.

body.html:
Jhansi’s first female auto driver, Anita Chaudhary (40), was found dead in a pool of blood near her overturned auto-rickshaw in the Navabad police station area early Sunday morning, triggering shock and outrage. The incident occurred around 1:30 am near Sukwan-Dhukwan Colony on Station Road.

Initially reported as a road accident, the case took a dramatic turn after a post-mortem confirmed that Anita was shot in the temple, with the bullet lodged in her neck. Police said the post-mortem was conducted by a panel of two doctors and videographed. The body was later handed over to the family.

Anita had left her home around 9:30 pm on Saturday to drive her auto. Her family alleged she had an argument with a young man known to her, who later killed her, robbed her jewellery and mobile phone, and tried to pass off the murder as an accident. The family also claimed two gunshots were fired.

City CO Laxmikant Gautam said police initially received information about an accident, but the family’s allegations are being thoroughly investigated. Based on the complaint, a murder case has been registered against Mukesh Jha, his brother-in-law, and others. Police said the accused will be arrested soon.

Anita, a resident of Ambedkar Nagar in Talpura, was widely known for breaking barriers by becoming Jhansi’s first woman auto driver in 2021. She was honoured by several organisations and senior police officers and inspired many women to take up auto and e-rickshaw driving. She is survived by three children.

articles.title: Tyre Burst Sends Car Crashing Into House in Karnataka, CCTV Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking road accident was caught on CCTV in Marakada, Karnataka, on January 1 at around 3:51 pm. A WagonR car reportedly lost control after a tyre burst and rammed straight into the wall of a house.

body.html:
A shocking road accident was caught on CCTV in Marakada, Karnataka, on January 1 at around 3:51 pm. A WagonR car reportedly lost control after a tyre burst and rammed straight into the wall of a house.

The viral footage shows the car suddenly veering off the road, entering the house premises, and crashing into the courtyard. Even after partially overturning, one of the tyres can be seen spinning, indicating the severity of the impact.

Local residents rushed to the spot within minutes and helped set the vehicle upright. Reportedly, the occupants escaped without serious injuries. The car was travelling from Neerude to Bondel, while the identities of those inside are yet to be confirmed.

articles.title: Drunk Driver’s Speeding Car Mows Down Bikes, Man Thrown in Air; CCTV Horror in Roorkee
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Panic gripped Roorkee in Uttarakhand’s Haridwar district after a speeding car driven by an allegedly drunk man rammed into two parked bikes and hit a young man outside a shop.

body.html:
Panic gripped Roorkee in Uttarakhand’s Haridwar district after a speeding car driven by an allegedly drunk man rammed into two parked bikes and hit a young man outside a shop. The incident occurred on Saturday, January 3, in the Ganganagar Kotwali area and was captured on CCTV, with the video now going viral on social media.

According to reports, the car was heading towards the market from Durga Chowk when, near Nehru Stadium, the driver attempted to take a turn. Instead, the vehicle suddenly accelerated and crashed into two bikes parked outside a shop. A man coming out of the shop was struck by the car and thrown several feet into the air, leaving him seriously injured.

Bystanders rushed the injured man to hospital and caught hold of the driver at the spot. Police said the driver was so heavily intoxicated that he could not even disclose his name for several hours. The damaged bikes and the car were seized by the police.

The injured shopkeeper, identified as Arun Kumar, has filed a complaint demanding strict action. Inspector Manohar Bhandari, in-charge of the Ganga Canal police station, confirmed that the driver was in an inebriated condition at the time of the incident and that an investigation is underway.

articles.title: “I’m a Cop’s Son”: Drunk Youth Thrashes Café Owner, Smashes Shop Near IIT Kanpur
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking incident in Kanpur, the son of a police inspector allegedly vandalised a café and assaulted its owner after being refused alcohol and asked to pay the food bill. The incident took place on Saturday night in the Kalyanpur police station area.

body.html:
In a shocking incident in Kanpur, the son of a police inspector allegedly vandalised a café and assaulted its owner after being refused alcohol and asked to pay the food bill. The incident took place on Saturday night in the Kalyanpur police station area.

According to police, Avinash Singh, son of a police inspector posted in Jalaun district, arrived at Literature Café near the IIT gate along with his friend Baua Purane alias Baua Sharma. Café owner Gyan Awasthi said both men were drunk and demanded alcohol after ordering food. When told that drinking was prohibited and asked to clear the bill, Avinash allegedly lost his temper.

The accused allegedly kicked and punched the café owner, abused him, and hit him on the head with a chair. He also threw tables and chairs outside the café and broke the glass, claiming, “I am the son of a police inspector, how dare you ask me for money.” The entire incident was captured on the café’s CCTV cameras.

Following a complaint, Kalyanpur police reached the spot, seized the CCTV footage, and registered a case. Both accused were arrested late at night near Kalyanpur Crossing and sent to jail. Police said Baua Purane has multiple criminal cases registered against him, while Avinash Singh had earlier been involved in a firing incident near the IIT campus.

articles.title: Illicit Affair Turns Fatal: Man Hacked to Death Outside Police Station in Andhra Pradesh
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking murder took place in full public view outside Tanakallu Police Station in Sri Sathya Sai district, where a man was brutally killed moments after being released from police custody.

body.html:
A shocking murder took place in full public view outside Tanakallu Police Station in Sri Sathya Sai district, where a man was brutally killed moments after being released from police custody.

The victim, Iswarappa, a resident of Marpurivandlapalli, was allegedly involved in an illicit relationship with the wife of Hari, a resident of Raghinapalli. Four days ago, Iswarappa reportedly took the woman away, following which her husband Hari lodged a missing complaint with the police.

Based on the complaint, police traced Iswarappa and brought him to Tanakallu Police Station for questioning. After completing formalities, he was released on bail.

However, as soon as Iswarappa stepped out of the police station premises, Hari allegedly attacked him with a hunting sickle and killed him on the spot. The incident created panic in the area, as it occurred right in front of police personnel.

Iswarappa’s family has alleged that a head constable at Tanakallu Police Station aided the accused in carrying out the murder. Police have taken the accused into custody and stated that a detailed investigation is underway. Further action will be taken based on the findings.

articles.title: Indian-Origin Woman Murdered in US, Accused Friend Arrested in Tamil Nadu After Fleeing America
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking murder case involving an Indian-origin woman has come to light from the United States. Nikita Godishala (27), who was living in Columbia, Maryland, was found murdered, with police suspecting her close friend Arjun Sharma (26) as the prime accused.

body.html:
A shocking murder case involving an Indian-origin woman has come to light from the United States. Nikita Godishala (27), who was living in Columbia, Maryland, was found murdered, with police suspecting her close friend Arjun Sharma (26) as the prime accused.

Nikita was reported missing on December 31 after Arjun Sharma approached the police, claiming he was the last person to see her in Ellicott City. However, his sudden departure to India after filing the complaint raised suspicion.

Following this, US police obtained a search warrant and searched Arjun’s apartment, where Nikita’s decomposed body was recovered. Multiple stab wounds were found on her body, confirming she had been brutally murdered.

Police identified Arjun Sharma as the main suspect and sought assistance from federal agencies after it was discovered that he had fled to India. Nikita is reported to have roots in the Secunderabad area.

In a major development, INTERPOL, in coordination with Indian agencies, arrested the accused Arjun Sharma in Tamil Nadu. Further legal proceedings and extradition formalities are underway.
